papers.inspection: Read abstract and architecture §2.1–2.4: Thinker/Talker, common temporal organization/TMRoPE and streaming codec decoder. No local inference claim.
Read abstract and architecture §2: Thinker/Talker, multi-codebook speech representation and causal ConvNet; published analysis distinguished from this course finite-tone product.
Read cached original PDF text: abstract, §3.1 eqs1–2 nearest embedding, §3.2 straight-through learning; supports codebook principle, not this course tone quality.
Read abstract, introduction/figure1 and architecture discussion of residual vector quantization; actual speech/audio codec objective is broader than finite sinusoidal tones.

inspection_notes.nanochat/README.md: Introduction and file map: complete LLM workflow and --depth complexity dial; no upstream speed/cost claim transferred to this course.
inspection_notes.nanochat/runs/runcpu.sh: Lines 3–10 explicitly call CPU/MPS educational; lines 27–65 cover tokenizer, six-layer base model, evaluation and chat_sft. Script was read, not executed.
inspection_notes.nanochat/runs/speedrun.sh: Lines 55–76 run tokenizer train/eval, pretrain, base_eval (CORE/BPB/samples), then chat_sft and chat_eval.
inspection_notes.nanochat/scripts/tok_eval.py: Lines 180–189 encode/decode exact roundtrip assertion, byte/token counts and compression ratio; comparison loop reports both tokenizers.
inspection_notes.nanochat/nanochat/loss_eval.py: evaluate_bpb lines 8–78 sums target-token nats, masks negative labels and zero-byte special tokens, and divides by log(2)*target bytes. Same-document/target-boundary requirements remain necessary.
inspection_notes.nanochat/nanochat/tokenizer.py: render_conversation lines 140–224 constructs parallel IDs/masks; visualize_tokenization lines 226–239 colors assistant-trained versus other tokens.
inspection_notes.nanochat/nanochat/gpt.py: Header and MLP lines 128–141 use Dense ReLU squared; token embedding and lm_head are separate untied modules. Attention uses rotary/GQA/cache/FA3 adapter.
inspection_notes.nanochat/nanochat/engine.py: KVCache class lines 82 onward, prefill(other) and Engine.generate lines 176 onward implement prompt prefill, cache clone and token generation.
inspection_notes.nanochat/nanochat/flash_attention.py: Module exports FA3-compatible flash_attn_func and flash_attn_with_kvcache, with SDPA fallback. Availability/performance on another device was not inferred.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/README.md: Training guide lines 244–260 recommends direct SFT and optional projector prealignment; lines 440–503 describe mixed caption/instruction/pure-text data, frozen SigLIP2 and partly unfrozen LLM. Line 342 explicitly distinguishes pretrained MiniMind backbone from a from-random VLM.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/model/model_vlm.py: MMVisionProjector; MiniMindVLM.get_vision_model lines 46–59 loads/fixes SigLIP2; count_vision_proj replaces image placeholder spans with projected features; forward shifts logits/labels and ignores -100.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/dataset/lm_dataset.py: VLMDataset.generate_labels lines 81–99 starts with -100 and copies assistant spans including EOS; __getitem__ renders roles, pads and returns labels.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/trainer/trainer_utils.py: init_vlm_model lines 66–95 loads existing LM state, freezes non-projector weights, and freeze_llm=1 re-enables first/last LLM layers; vision stays frozen.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/trainer/train_pretrain_vlm.py: Argument definitions lines 100–102: from_weight=llm, freeze_llm=2; main passes that freeze strategy into init_vlm_model.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/trainer/train_sft_vlm.py: Lines 100–102 set SFT from_weight=pretrain_vlm and freeze_llm=1; README supplies the direct-from-llm alternative. The statement is about default freezing, not compulsory prealignment.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/scripts/web_demo_vlm.py: Imports Gradio line 9; launch_gradio_server lines 117–154 uses Blocks, Chatbot, image-capable MultimodalTextbox and launch.
inspection_notes.minimind-v/model/model_minimind.py: Config lines 25/30 defaults hidden_act=silu and tie_word_embeddings=True; FeedForward lines 140–146 gates up_proj by activated gate_proj; line 247 aliases embedding/lm_head weights.
inspection_notes.minimind/README.md: Sections Knowledge Distillation lines 735–751 distinguish teacher-generated-answer black-box SFT and distribution CE+KL white-box KD; LoRA section lines 760 onward describes low-rank adapters and identity/domain adaptation examples.
inspection_notes.minimind/trainer/train_dpo.py: logits_to_log_probs and dpo_loss lines 24–50 gather chosen/rejected log probabilities, apply masks and compare policy/reference ratios; reference forward under no_grad.
inspection_notes.minimind/model/model_minimind.py: FeedForward and MOEFeedForward lines 134–180: Dense gated FFN versus top-k routed experts; auxiliary load/importance balancing term. Full expert ModuleList exists even when only selected experts execute.
inspection_notes.minimind/trainer/train_distillation.py: distillation_loss lines 25–36 uses detached teacher softmax, student log_softmax, KL and T squared; train_epoch lines 49–91 shifts targets, masks ignored tokens and combines CE/KD. This code was read, never executed.
inspection_notes.smol-course/units/en/unit1/1.md: What is Instruction Tuning and Module Overview explicitly frame SFT as adapting a pretrained base for instruction/chat behavior.
inspection_notes.smol-course/units/en/unit1/3.md: SFT teaching section and implementation guide explain supervised conversational examples and separate training/evaluation; no SmolLM3 quality claim is imported.
inspection_notes.smol-course/units/en/unit2/1.md: Introduction to Preference Alignment separates instruction SFT from preference optimization and describes DPO without a separately trained reward model.
inspection_notes.smol-course/units/en/unit2/2.md: DPO algorithm/format sections describe prompt, chosen/rejected response pairs and reference-model comparison; source supports the preference-training role only.
inspection_notes.safe-rlhf/README.md: Lines 58–76 define helpfulness reward maximization with safety-cost constraint, and separate neural human-proxy reward/cost functions.
inspection_notes.ao/README.md: Project overview separates quantization/inference and QAT/training tools, with support/backend qualifications; no unsupported universal speed guarantee is inferred.
inspection_notes.ao/docs/source/contributing/quantization: Stack diagram and Basic DTypes/Primitive Ops/Efficient kernels/Quantized Tensors sections separate numerical low precision, packing (two int4 per uint8) and kernels.
inspection_notes.ao/docs/source/workflows/qat.md: Lines 3–28 distinguish fake quantization from casting/storage and define prepare, train and convert; API examples inspected without execution.
inspection_notes.pytorch/docs/source/notes/autograd.rst: Autograd mechanics opening describes graph construction and reverse chain-rule differentiation; only used for the generic figure interpretation.
inspection_notes.pytorch/torch/optim/optimizer.py: Optimizer.zero_grad line 1028 onward resets gradients, default set_to_none=True; gradient accumulation policy must be controlled by caller.
inspection_notes.lora: LoRA v2 abstract and section 4: freeze pretrained W0 and optimize low-rank BA; fewer trainable parameters does not imply fewer stored base weights or guaranteed task quality.
